Is it audio/video quality? Gameplay skill? Insightful, informative, or humorous commentary? Or do you just like to see people having fun? Discuss!
So what does everyone like to see most in a Let's Play?
To me, the two big things are audio/video quality, and having strong commentary. Gameplay skill will come as the lets play continues.

I'm a fan of audio/video quality and engaging banter. It's hard for me to get into a channel that is only one guy because there isn't much for them to riff off of. With that said, I have seen channels that comprise of a single person that pulls off good commentary quite well, and, for me, that's what separates the good channels from the bad. Listening to someone make noises and "oooh!"-ing and "aaaaagh!!!"-ing for ten to thirty minutes doesn't do it for me. Personal preferences and what-not.

I think as long as your audio and video quality are decent they'll be fine for the vast majority of people - not too many are turned off by imperfections as long as it isn't glaringly annoying. Being interesting/fun/relatable/informative is crucial, and I think a lot of people watch for the fun factor.

To me though, it has to be accompanied by some level of competence, even if it's a blind run you need to be decent at the game or it turns me off. I don't want to watch you fail constantly or miss obvious information/clues/controls. I tend more toward non-blind LPs because of this, but certain people like ChristopherOdd tend to be naturally good at gaming - so their blind runs are usually satisfying.

Of the couple of people I regularly watch, the reason I found them was searching to improve my skill at a game. That said, that isn't enough to keep me as a viewer for more than videos on that game while I'm interested. For that, it's more about entertaining commentary.

No, KIA started because of gamergate. Your understanding of said topic is going to be heavily skewed depending on how deeply involved you are in said conversation, but let me try and give a brief non bias explanation.

GG claims to be about ethics in gaming journalism, which I agree with. Most of the people within the movement hold a similar belief. Now you might ask yourself whats wrong with that and why is it a big controversy? Well the people who are at odds with GG, antiGG or whatever you want to call them, claim that GG is all about misogyny and harassing women out of gaming space. I personally find that to be an outrageous claim, and I encourage you to dig DEEPLY into the topic if you are interested, the KIA sidebar on reddit and voat has a lot of good info to get started.

KIA started when a bunch of gaming websites posted a series of articles, at the same time, claiming the gaming identity was dead (of which Kotaku was one, hence the name of the sub). People who have been passionate about gaming and considered themselves gamers were bad people accorinding to these articles, in not so nice of words. Not only was it upsetting to many MANY gamers, it also brought accusations of collusion to light and a lot of those accusations were later verified (see the gamejournopros mailing list).

Many of the people against GG identify with the SJW mentality, and many people within GG strongly oppose that mentality. KIA has been sort of a front line in a culture clash, and a lot of topics on KIA have to do with battles with that mentality. A lot of time there is overlap with gaming topics, but sometimes there is not and you will see post simply ridiculing the SJW mentality like you might see on tumblerinaction.

Although that kind of stuff does show up on KIA from time to time the main point has been ethical standards in gaming journalism, and the culture battle within the gaming sphere. It has also spilled into fighting against censorship in other fandoms (like comics and Sci-fi) and even ethics in normal journalism. Brigading is not encouraged or even permitted as far as I am aware, but mailing campaignes to sponsors of journalism websites we find corrupt are organised.

Here is where things get pretty opinionated, so fair warning, but I believe there is a LOT of purposeful misinformation spread to discredit gamergate. Claims that is a moment based in mysogyny are used to deflect from the actual issues, and make it seem like there is a clear "bad guys" side to this whole debate. Myogyny is easy to understand for the masses, who might be ill informed or simply not care about the ethical and censorship issues, so it's an easy narrative to push to make their side look credible.

Sorry for the long post, I hope that gives you somewhat of an idea.
